description: SASRec predicts the next item by using causal self-attention to select relevant interactions from a user's history. It combines item and position embeddings, attention blocks, and feed-forward layers, then scores candidates through embedding dot products. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1)
motivation: Attention allows predictions to emphasize recent actions in sparse histories while using longer-range dependencies when sufficient evidence exists. The supplied task applies this established method to four Amazon categories; no new cold-start mechanism is specified.
implementation_notes: Start from sasrec_perdataset and retain category routing. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the environment's 200-epoch default. Select using macro validation HR@10 across all four categories. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader). Update the predictor writer whenever architecture changes. SASRec alone does not provide representations for unseen items without training interactions; using available titles or descriptions would require an additional proposed mechanism.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged training split.
  Left-pad or truncate interaction histories.
  Encode item and positional embeddings with causal attention.
  Score shifted positive items and sampled negatives.
  Optimize binary cross-entropy over valid positions.
  Save model configuration and weights beneath the trial directory.
Write a predictor that routes categories and reconstructs each trained model.
Use host validation HR@10 macro-average for selection.

originality.positive: Provides a clear, established sequential recommendation baseline.
originality.negative: The supplied description specifies benchmark constraints rather than a novel method.

future_potential.positive: Available item text could support a future content-based extension for sparse items.
future_potential.negative: Such an extension is unspecified and its validation benefit remains unmeasured.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing SASRec baseline supplies the main training and inference structure.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require synchronized predictor serialization and compatible diagnostic probes.
